title: Crows, a charioteer, and the fall of the Serapeum
english: The holy bishop Epiphanius told this story: In the time of blessed Athanasius the Great, crows were flying around the temple of Serapis, crying out without stopping, "Cras, cras." The pagans came to blessed Athanasius and shouted, "Evil old man, tell us what the crows are crying." He answered, "The crows are crying, 'Cras, cras.' In the language of the Ausonians, 'cras' means 'tomorrow.'" And he added, "Tomorrow you will see the glory of God." The next day the death of the emperor Julian was announced. When this happened, they ran together and shouted against Serapis, saying, "If you did not want him, why did you take what was his?"

The same one told this story: There was a charioteer in Alexandria who was the son of a woman named Mary. During a horse race he fell. Then he got up, passed the one who had thrown him down, and won. The crowd shouted, "The son of Mary has fallen and has risen and has won." While this cry was still being said, the report about the temple of Serapis reached the crowd: the great Theophilus had gone up, destroyed the idol of Serapis, and become master of the temple.

It was reported to blessed Epiphanius, the bishop of Cyprus, by the abba of the monastery he had in Palestine: "By your prayers we have not neglected our rule, but with diligence we perform the third, the sixth, and the ninth hours."
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The collection opens with Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus, telling stories about the fall of the Serapeum and the death of Julian, then a report from his monastery in Palestine.
